identity.exchangeName: Nebius Group N.V. - Class A Ordinary Shares

risks: Large contracted commitments require substantial timely capacity buildout and create customer concentration/execution exposure.
Rapid infrastructure scaling remains capital intensive and leverage increases fixed obligations.
Power, GPU supply, construction and commissioning become successor bottlenecks after demand is contracted.
Customer concentration and buildout timing can turn contracted backlog into financing stress if delivery slips.
GPU-cloud competition and hyperscaler self-build can pressure renewal economics and pricing.

Very rapid infrastructure scaling and the gap between adjusted EBITDA and GAAP net results require Alpha to test capital intensity, financing burden and quality of earnings rather than extrapolate top-line growth.
Preferred-partner status and technical integration do not establish committed revenue, utilization, margin or customer conversion.
Large contracted capacity requires substantial buildout and execution; headline contract value is not equivalent to near-term revenue, free cash flow or margin.

The announced model is a business architecture, not evidence of realized partner economics, deployment volumes, margin contribution or customer utilization; issuer characterization of high margins remains forward-looking until reported results exist.

The financing is secured by GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows, increasing asset encumbrance, while the very large Meta relationship creates material customer-concentration and delivery-execution exposure.
Convertible financing materially expands capital access but adds future repayment and potential dilution exposure; the 5 GW deployment objective is a forward target, not achieved capacity.
Secured debt introduces leverage and collateral dependence; the issuer does not disclose the customer identity, deployment-level return, utilization or downside economics in this announcement.
Dynamic spot pricing can improve utilization but the source provides no realized utilization uplift, revenue contribution, gross-margin effect or cannibalization data.
Secured financing adds leverage and depends on contracted cash flows and underlying infrastructure performance.
Q2 operating loss remained $175.9M and depreciation/amortization reached $259.7M as GPU and data-center investment scaled; rapid growth remains capital intensive.

The announcement does not disclose contract value, committed capacity, customer volumes, revenue contribution, margins or conversion timing; preferred-partner status is therefore distribution evidence rather than quantified economics.
Municipal incentive-plan approval enables construction but does not establish completed capacity, energization timing, utilization, customer revenue, project returns or final delivered economics.
Potential 1.2 GW scale can overstate near-term economic capacity if construction, energization, customer ramp or utilization lag the plan.

The financing is secured by infrastructure and contracted cash flows, adding leverage and asset encumbrance; issuer-stated capex coverage does not establish returns across the broader $20B-$25B 2026 capex program.
If secured financing expands faster than durable contracted cash generation, leverage and asset encumbrance could reduce funding resilience across the broader buildout.
Integration timing, customer conversion and economics were not quantified in the announcement.
Preferred-partner status is not equivalent to committed revenue and must not be valued as contracted backlog without disclosure.
Valuing the partnership as committed demand would inflate confidence because conversion, timing, margins and customer uptake remain undisclosed.
Secured financing encumbers underlying infrastructure and introduces SOFR-linked debt service.
Execution still depends on deployment timing, GPU availability, power and customer performance.
Partnership economics and realized customer conversion were not disclosed in the announcement.
Strategic designation is not itself evidence of booked revenue or utilization.
The arrangement requires large-scale capacity buildout and the additional-capacity commitment does not mean all $15 billion will necessarily be purchased.
Execution depends on timely construction, equipment deployment and energization of capacity.
Preferred-partner status and planned integration do not quantify committed revenue, customer adoption or capacity utilization.
Execution requires successful integration and conversion of eligible Palantir customers into paid Nebius usage.
The financing adds substantial convertible debt and therefore future interest, refinancing and potential dilution/overhang considerations belong in Alpha underwriting.
The company exchanged $800 million aggregate principal of older convertible notes for approximately 15.8 million Class A shares, creating an explicit equity-supply/dilution consideration.
Capital availability does not prove that capacity can be built on time or monetized at attractive returns.
Convertible structure can transfer part of execution risk into future dilution or balance-sheet burden.
A planned 328 MW deployment is not proof of commissioned capacity, sustained availability, delivered power cost, or economics at Nebius load factors.
Behind-the-meter generation diversifies one bottleneck but does not remove GPU, construction, interconnection, fuel-supply, commissioning, or customer-utilization execution risk.
The operating target remains forward-looking until commissioning evidence confirms delivered capacity.
Fast time-to-power does not by itself establish attractive unit economics or full data-center readiness.
The ten-vote Class B structure concentrates voting power relative to economic ownership and can reduce ordinary Class A holders' influence over governance outcomes.

Five-year authority to issue up to an additional 20% of issued share capital, together with authority to exclude pre-emption rights, creates a material dilution/governance option even though it does not establish that shares will be issued.
Financing flexibility is not realized operating execution; future equity issuance could dilute Class A holders and should not be counted as deployed capital or completed capacity.
